disputes.reason: ambiguous 'gap': in Hull Table 9.5 the absolute difference widens but the ratio of spread-implied to historical hazard rate narrows for riskier ratings, so 'smaller ... closer to actuarial cost' can reasonably be read as true; label and explanation depend on which measure is meant.

defensible as true: under a classic CSA the independent amount is added into the single credit support amount (eq. 17.2), so initial and variation margin can be netted into one transfer; falseness holds only for segregated regulatory IM.

claim that excess IM is returned in a transfer separate from VM is not a general rule (IA is netted in a combined credit support amount under classic CSAs); explanation also does not support the claim.
the example '2% of notional if downgraded to BBB+' depends on the question's specific rating-linked schedule, which the student never sees, so the statement cannot be judged as written.
